response.why: batch: player A starts
0 lands in hand. Cannot cast any spell turn 1 with no mana. Aggro deck needs to start dealing damage immediately — a blank turn 1 is unacceptable. Mulligan for a hand with 2+ lands and early plays.

Mulligan to 6: bottom a Mountain. With 4 Mountains in 7 cards (67% lands), I'm mana-heavy. Keep 3 lands + 2 hasty creatures (Swiftspear and Challenger) + Shock. Aggro needs velocity and threats; 3 Mountains is sufficient mana, and bottoming a land reduces flood probability while preserving my payoffs.

Keep. 3 Mountains (solid mana base), 2 hasty creatures that attack immediately (Swiftspear and Challenger with Prowess synergy), 1 burn spell for reach or removal. This is an ideal aggressive curve for a 6-card hand—no mulligan needed.
Turn 1 precombat main: always play my land first. I have 3 Mountains and have not played a land this turn. After this, I can cast Monastery Swiftspear ({R} with Haste) to attack immediately.

Cast Monastery Swiftspear. It costs {R} (paid by my untapped Mountain), has Haste (attacks this turn), and is the primary threat for aggro turn 1. This starts the clock and sets up Prowess synergy with future spells.

Leaf 0 (no attack): Passive position, both at 20 life. Aggro needs to apply clock every turn—passing is behind my game plan. Leaf 1 (attack): Deal 1 damage (opp to 19), Swiftspear tapped but safe (opponent has no blockers or threats). Attacking is always correct when free; advances my race clock immediately.

Pass priority. I'm on turn 3, no creatures on board yet. Hold Shock for their creatures (likely flyers like Deep-Cavern Bat that I can't block). Better to enter main phase and deploy Emberheart Challenger, then hold Shock as versatile removal or reach for the race. Casting it now wastes the instant speed flexibility.
Draw step—just drew Monstrous Rage. No action needed in draw phase. Pass to main phase where I can play lands and cast Emberheart Challenger. Hold Shock for their creatures.

Opponent's main phase. They have Faerie Mastermind (2/2 flying). While it's a threat, it's summoning sick (can't attack this turn), and I need Shock for bigger threats (Deep-Cavern Bat, removal heavy deck). Pass and hold Shock. I'll race them—their flying won't be faster than my 2/2 Haste creature.
Begin combat phase, opponent's turn. Faerie Mastermind is summoning sick (can't attack). Opponent likely has no attackers. No reason to act—pass and move toward their postcombat main phase.
Declare attackers phase. Opponent has only Faerie Mastermind, which is summoning sick (cannot attack this turn). No legal attackers. Pass through this phase.
End combat phase. No combat occurred (opponent had no attackers). Pass through to their postcombat main phase.
Opponent's postcombat main. They have 5 cards in hand and may play a creature or pass. I'll hold priority windows to respond with Shock if they deploy a threat. Pass for now.
End turn. Opponent passed without playing spells on turn 4. Now it's my turn 5—time to play my creatures and attack. Pass to my upkeep.
Upkeep—nothing to do. Pass to draw step.
Draw step. Drew Burst Lightning. No action needed in draw phase—pass to main phase where I can play lands and creatures.

Precombat main, turn 5: always play my land first. I have 2 Mountains in hand and haven't played a land this turn. Play Mountain, then I'll have 2 untapped Mountains + 1 tapped Mountain and mana to cast Emberheart Challenger.

Cast Emberheart Challenger ({1}{R}, 2/2 Haste). I have 2 untapped Mountains to pay the cost. It attacks immediately this turn (Haste), applying pressure while still holding up Shock for their threats.

Leaf 0 (no attack): Passive, no progress. Leaf 1 (they block, trade): Both creatures die, empty board, opponent has hand advantage—bad for aggro. Leaf 2 (unblocked): Deal 2 damage (opponent to 17), creature survives, clock ticks—best outcome. Attacking is correct: even trading is acceptable when it advances my pace, and unblocked is a win. Attack.

No-blocks leaf: Opponent's Faerie Mastermind dealt 2 unblocked damage (me to 18), now tapped. Blocking would trade my creature for theirs—bad for aggro with hand disadvantage. Keeping my Emberheart Challenger alive and their creature tapped is the right play. Next turn I attack again while they develop. Position is good—ahead on active threats.
Upkeep—nothing to do. Pass to draw step.
Draw step. Drew another Mountain. Pass to main phase to play lands and creatures.

Precombat main turn 7: play my land first. I have 2 Mountains in hand and haven't played a land this turn. After this, I'll have 3 untapped Mountains and can cast Emberheart Challenger or pump it with Monstrous Rage, then attack.

Precombat main: pass priority to move to combat. I have 3 untapped Mountains, Emberheart Challenger ready to attack, and opponent's Faerie Mastermind is tapped (can't block). Attack now to apply clock.
Begin combat—pass priority to move to declare attackers phase. I'll attack with Emberheart Challenger (opponent's Faerie Mastermind is tapped and can't block).

Leaf 0 (no attack): Passive position, no clock progress, wasting my creature. Leaf 1 (attack unblocked): Deal 2 damage (opponent to 17 life), creature survives and untaps next turn. My clock is ticking while their Faerie Mastermind is tapped. Strong tempo—attack.
Declare attackers: Emberheart Challenger is already tapped and declared (attack already chosen). Pass to blockers phase.
Opponent's turn 8 upkeep. My creature dealt 2 damage (them at 17). No need to respond; pass and see what they play.
Opponent's draw phase. No response needed. Pass and continue.
Opponent's main phase with open mana. Holding instant-speed burn for reactive use (combat tricks, protection, or damage when they're tapped). Pass to preserve options.
Faerie Mastermind attacking. Shock kills it before it deals 2 damage. Efficient use of instant removal.
Kill Faerie Mastermind before it deals combat damage.
Let Shock resolve. No additional response needed in combat.

Play Mountain. This is my land drop for the turn, develops mana for future plays.
Opponent's precombat main phase, turn 10. Pass priority to see their action. No immediate response needed.

End of opponent's turn 10. No damage dealt this turn. Pass to begin my turn 11.
Pass upkeep. No effects to resolve.

Leaf 0 (pass): Falls behind as Enduring Curiosity threatens next turn. Leaf 1 (blocked, bad response): Worst case loses creature without progress. Leaf 2 (unblocked): Best case—deals 1 damage (17→16), Hired Claw survives tapped, pushes clock. Leaf 3 (blocked, trade): Eliminates Drowner via response spell but loses Hired Claw. Must attack to stay competitive in race; leaf 2 alone justifies it.

Cast Lightning Bolt on Floodpits Drowner. Removes their only reliable blocker preemptively, letting Hired Claw attack unblocked for 1 damage (17→16). Costs 1R from my 3 available mana. Maximizes pressure in tight race.
Kill Floodpits Drowner. It's their only immediate blocker. Removes blocker, allows Hired Claw to attack unblocked for 1 damage.
Pass priority. Let Lightning Bolt resolve and kill Floodpits Drowner, then proceed to declare Hired Claw as attacker.
Pass priority. Lightning Bolt killed Floodpits Drowner. Now declare Hired Claw as attacker, getting through unblocked (Enduring Curiosity is summoning sick).

Cast Monstrous Rage targeting Enduring Curiosity. Kills their only threat and removes their blocker. Costs {1}{R}, I have 3 untapped Mountains. Clears the board for my next turn's attack.
Target Enduring Curiosity. Removes their primary threat and clears the board for my next turn's attacks with Hired Claw.

Pass opponent's draw step. Let them proceed to main phase where their threats will materialize.
Pass opponent's precombat main phase. Wait to see if they play threats before using Burst Lightning. They have limited resources with only 1 card in hand.

Pass to combat. Opponent just cast a second Enduring Curiosity (4/3 with summoning sickness). Burst Lightning won't kill either creature, so saving it for combat interaction is better. Need to evaluate blocking opportunities.

Pass declare attackers. Opponent attacking with 5/4 Enduring Curiosity. Move to blockers phase to evaluate what can block the flying attacker.

Blocking with Hired Claw is better than taking 5 unblocked. Option 1 (no-blocks) leaves me at 13 life facing 5+4=9 damage next turn (certain death in 2 turns). Option 2 (block) leaves me at 15 life and reduces next turn's damage to just 4 (buying an extra turn). In a losing race, delaying matters. Block.

Pass priority and proceed to declare blockers. I'll block the attacking 5/4 Enduring Curiosity with Hired Claw. Casting Burst Lightning now won't kill the 5/4 (only deals 2 damage), so it's better to save resources and block.

Cast Manifold Mouse (1/2 creature). I'm at 15 life vs 17, losing the race. Need to put pressure on the board. If it has haste, I can attack this turn and threaten damage. Burst Lightning alone won't stabilize.
Pay {2} for offspring token. Good outcome indicated. Creates additional pressure on opponent and improves board presence in this close race.
Choose double strike. My creatures are small (Manifold Mouse is 1/1). Double strike turns my 1/1 into 2 damage per combat, crucial in this close race where I'm at 15 vs opponent 17 life.

Leaf 0 (no blocks): Take 9 damage, go to 6 life - nearly dead next turn. Leaf 1 (block, 1 dmg reduction): Go to 7 life - marginal improvement. Choose leaf 2: blocks reduce damage most effectively, keeping me alive longer to draw into more burn.

Target opponent directly with Lightning Bolt (3 damage). In a losing race at 10 vs 17 life, every damage to the opponent matters more than removing creatures. Opponent's creatures will continue attacking regardless; racing their life total is my only path.

Cast Burst Lightning (2 damage to opponent). After Lightning Bolt, opponent is at 14 life. Casting Burst Lightning brings them to 12. I need to maximize burn damage in this race before opponent's creatures untap and attack for lethal next turn.

Paying 4 mana to deal extra damage via kicker doesn't change the outcome - I still die to opponent's 5/4 + 4/3 + 4/3 attack next turn (~13 damage). Better to cast base Burst Lightning (2 damage) and preserve resources for potential future turns.

Targeting creatures doesn't help the race—creatures won't die to 2 damage, and I can't remove the threat before they attack next turn anyway. Only direct damage matters in this race.
